keyframe_review.note: 638-643: 73,965 km2, which is the Caucasian Albania 509 outline (285 cells; only 9 differ from Albania 509). The Balasagan page places the region 'in the area of the Kura and Aras rivers, adjacent to the Caspian Sea' with its heartland the Dasht i-Balasakan, 'which corresponds to the Mughan plain', and calls it a separate entity from Caucasian Albania though 'virtually subject to Albania'. The page gives no area; the whole-Albania outline is about seven times the Mughan plain, so the shape is trimmed to the Mughan (about 11,000 km2). The rest of the Cliopatria outline (Albania proper) is Sasanian land in 510-645 in the sasanian-empire dossier (gain 510).

notes:
WHAT THIS ROW IS: Cliopatria's Balasagan (638..646, two shapes of 74,000 km2) is the Caucasian Albania 509 outline almost cell for cell, but the Balasagan page describes a region on the Mughan plain, 'virtually subject to Albania', and says 'Nothing is known about the Kingdom of Balasagan'. The dossier therefore trims both shapes to the Mughan (about 11,000 km2) and treats the state as a Sasanian province or vassal kingdom conquered by the Arabs c. 645. If the orchestrator prefers not to draw a state here, the dossier can be dropped; the Albanian lowlands 510-645 are then Sasanian land in the sasanian-empire dossier (gain 510) and 645-646 Rashidun.

START AND END: 638 is Cliopatria's (the province is attested from the 3rd century, but the page has no continuous history); 645 is the page's c. 645 (Cliopatria 646). Not recorded: the Sasanian take-over of Balasagan 'from their Albanian vassals in the 5th-century (or possibly as early as 387)', Sanesan of Maskut occupying a portion c. 335/6, Heran's part in crushing the 450-451 Armenian rebellion: all precede the dossier's life and the page's dates for them are partly reign spans.

NO CAPITAL: the page names none.

GAZETTEER: no name for the Mughan plain (Mughan, Mugan, Dasht i-Balasakan); a 90 km disk at 48.6E 39.55N stands in for it. Needed: region 'Mughan plain'.

PAGE BUDGET: 2 pages (Balasagan, Caucasian Albania). The Balasagan text came back without an infobox, so capital, area and succession fields are unverified. The second Caucasian Albania fetch gave the Arran triangle ('formed by the junction of the Kura and Aras rivers ... Mil plain and parts of the Mughan plain') as the Islamic-era extent.
